claims.statement: For programme purposes, orientation is modelled as a temporally extended agent-world-action relation.
claims.strongestCase: It preserves embodiment, environmental constraint and temporal coupling that isolated belief inventories omit.
claims.strongestRival: An internally realized predictive-control model can represent all relevant external variables without adopting a relational ontology.
claims.challenge: Show a consequence beyond relabelling inputs as relations.
claims.thirdOrderAudit: The definition may make every result appear compatible with the programme.

claims.statement: In some skilled tasks, preregistered relational state variables predict coupling perturbation, restoration and transfer better out of sample than an equally constrained enriched internal predictive-control model.
claims.scope: Task-bounded model comparison, not all cognition
assumptions: perturbation separates contingency from novelty and difficulty
losses: model superiority does not settle metaphysical constitution
task success does not generalize to all orientation
claims.strongestCase: Action-contingent organization may contain predictive structure lost by component-wise internal descriptions.
claims.strongestRival: A sufficiently rich internal generative model predicts the same coupling dependence.
claims.challenge: Outperform I1 without post hoc relational variables or parameter advantage.
claims.thirdOrderAudit: The programme is linguistically and theoretically invested in a relational victory.
claims.retirementRule: Retire or narrow if I1 matches R1 across preregistered held-out perturbation and transfer tasks.

claims.statement: Representational demands produce expertise-, task-, timing- and prompt-dependent gains, losses or null effects rather than a universal degradation of tacit skill.
assumptions: performance and report quality measured independently
losses: incomplete report does not prove ineffability
performance cost does not prove constitutive externalism
claims.strongestCase: Explicit monitoring, planning and instruction show heterogeneous effects across studies and tasks.
claims.strongestRival: Observed effects are generic dual-task load or demand characteristics.
claims.challenge: Identify mechanism-specific interactions beyond generic cognitive load.
claims.thirdOrderAudit: Tacit knowledge can be romanticized to shield expertise from scrutiny.

claims.statement: Institutions eliciting tacit knowledge should preserve practitioner contestability while permitting performance-based challenge and safety review.
assumptions: practitioner and affected-party interests may diverge
losses: contestability can add cost and delay
performance measures can themselves distort practice
claims.strongestCase: Both extraction and guild closure create predictable epistemic and power failures.
claims.strongestRival: Clear expert hierarchy or standardized measurement may be safer in high-stakes domains.
claims.challenge: Specify when contestability improves outcomes rather than merely distributing vetoes.
claims.thirdOrderAudit: The proposal may project the programme's preference for corrigibility into every institution.
